s1.syndrome_frame: febrile illness with multi-organ involvement and inflammatory response
salient_findings: tenderness in the left lower quadrant
dense atypical lymphoid infiltrate on peritoneal biopsy
key_facts: four days of fevers, fatigue, nausea, headaches, and malaise
blood pressure of 82/50 mm Hg (responded to fluids)
peritoneal biopsy showed dense atypical lymphoid infiltrate
immunohistochemistry positive for CD3, CD8, CD7, CD43, CD5 (partial loss), TIA-1, granzyme B, CD2, and TCRβ F1

shortlist.label: Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: elevated ferritin, fever, and multi-organ involvement

shortlist.label: Subcutaneous panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: peritoneal biopsy showed dense atypical lymphoid infiltrate and immunohistochemistry positive for T-cell markers

shortlist.label: Systemic EBV-positive T-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: elevated interleukin (IL)-2R alpha levels and atypical lymphoid infiltrate

shortlist.label: T-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: immunohistochemistry positive for T-cell markers and multi-organ involvement

shortlist.label: Macrophage activation syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: elevated ferritin, fever, and multi-organ involvement, similar to hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with fever, fatigue, and malaise, along with laboratory findings of elevated liver enzymes, ferritin, and LDH, and a peritoneal biopsy showing dense atypical lymphoid infiltrate with immunohistochemistry positive for CD3, CD8, and other T-cell markers, is most consistent with Subcutaneous panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma. The presence of systemic symptoms and the specific immunophenotypic profile further support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis
rejected.why: Although the bone marrow biopsy suggested HLH and the patient had elevated ferritin and LDH, the peritoneal biopsy findings and immunohistochemistry results are more specific for a T-cell lymphoma

rejected.label: Systemic EBV-positive T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: There is no mention of EBV positivity in the vignette, making this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: This is a broader category that includes Subcutaneous panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma, but the specific findings in this case make the more specific diagnosis more appropriate

rejected.label: Macrophage activation syndrome
rejected.why: This condition is often associated with autoimmune disorders and the presence of a dense atypical lymphoid infiltrate is not typical of macrophage activation syndrome
